title: The Solution Structure and Dynamics of Full-length Human Cerebral Dopamine Neurotrophic Factor and Its Neuroprotective Role against α-Synuclein Oligomers.
experiment: 15N R1 and R2 spin relaxation (800 MHz in Experimental Procedures; 600 MHz in Fig. 2 legend) and TROSY-based steady-state 15N{1H}-NOE (600 MHz)
buffer: 20 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM NaCl, 3 mM NaN3, 1 mM EDTA, and 10% (v/v) D2O
other_conditions: 0.65 mM CDNF; monomeric in solution; R2/R1 structured-domain averages: 14.4 ± 5.7 s-1 for N-terminal domain (residues 17-24, 34-37, 39-46, 52-58, 74-78) and 10.7 ± 3.2 s-1 for C-terminal domain (residues 113, 118-129, 139-150), indicating faster overall tumbling of the C-terminal domain; overall {1H}-15N NOE average = 0.70; residues 2 and 3 excluded due to signal overlap
alt_state_structure: 4BIT: solution NMR ensemble of monomeric full-length CDNF with partially folded alpha-helix 4 (solvent-exposed Ala-66 and Leu-70) and semi-independently oriented N- and C-terminal domains (Fig. 1, Fig. 3, Table 1); 2W50: X-ray crystal structure of dimeric N-terminal CDNF (residues 1-107) with well-defined alpha-helical residues 65-73 and buried Ala-66 and Leu-70 side chains (Fig. 3, Results)
author_claim: R2/R1 and steady-state {1H}-15N NOE measurements show semi-independent tumbling of the N-terminal (residues 10-100) and C-terminal (residues 111-157) domains, fast ps-ns thermal fluctuations in N-terminal residues 4-9, C-terminal residues K158-L161, central linker residues 103-113 ({1H}-15N NOE < 0.70), and individual residues S33, L34, T48, L55, and A66, as well as ns-ms motions (R2/R1 variation without {1H}-15N NOE decrease) in L41, C45, L46, G60, D112, L125, Y141, Y152, A154, and T155.
anchor: The dynamics data are compiled on the surface map shown in E and F, using a color scheme to indicate residues with low flexibility (no significant change of measured values: blue), intermediate flexibility (line width broadening: yellow), intermediate to fast flexibility (variation in R2/R1 but not in {1H}-15N NOE: orange), and fast to very fast flexibility (significant decrease of {1H}-15N NOE: red).
locator: Fig. 2C-F and legend (p. 20533), Results pp. 20531-20534; conditions: Experimental Procedures, Protein Production and NMR Experiments (p. 20529)
caveat_note: Internal field discrepancy: Experimental Procedures (p. 20529) states R1 and R2 were measured at 800 MHz and steady-state 15N{1H}-NOE at 600 MHz (at 25 °C), whereas Fig. 2 legend (p. 20533) states R2/R1 and 15N{1H}-NOE data were collected at 600 MHz at 298 K. Deposit comparison: the RelaxDB card for CDNFSP specifies the 101-residue saposin-like domain (sequence_length = 101, sheet_temperature_K = 298.0, sheet_field_MHz = 800, blank pH and sample components), whereas this paper measured full-length CDNF-(1-161) (BMRB 19164); whether the CDNFSP deposit was sliced from this full-length 800 MHz dataset or measured on an isolated domain cannot be verified from paper.txt alone. On p. 20532, dimensionless R2/R1 averages are printed with units s-1 (14.4 ± 5.7 and 10.7 ± 3.2 s-1). Endpoint one-letter codes for ranges 4-9 and 103-113 are not printed in paper.txt.

title: The Solution Structure and Dynamics of Full-length Human Cerebral Dopamine Neurotrophic Factor and Its Neuroprotective Role against α-Synuclein Oligomers.
experiment: 2D [15N,1H]-HSQC 1H amide line-width measurement at 1 GHz and backbone HN resonance broadening/absence at 600, 800, and 1000 MHz
buffer: 20 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM NaCl, 3 mM NaN3, 1 mM EDTA, and 10% (v/v) D2O
other_conditions: 0.65 mM CDNF; monomeric in solution; regime (authors): intermediate chemical exchange (millisecond time scale); structured-core 1H line-width averages at 1 GHz: 30 Hz for N-terminal domain (residues 17-24, 34-37, 39-46, 52-58, 74-78) and 25 Hz for C-terminal domain (residues 113, 118-129, 139-150)
alt_state_structure: 4BIT: solution NMR ensemble of monomeric full-length CDNF with partially folded alpha-helix 4 (solvent-exposed Ala-66 and Leu-70) and semi-independently oriented N- and C-terminal domains (Fig. 1, Fig. 3, Table 1); 2W50: X-ray crystal structure of dimeric N-terminal CDNF (residues 1-107) with well-defined alpha-helical residues 65-73 and buried Ala-66 and Leu-70 side chains (Fig. 3, Results)
author_claim: Extreme broadening or absence of backbone amide proton resonances in C11-E16, K68-R75 (N-terminal region of alpha-helix 4), E88, linker residues E99-K101, C132-R133 (with A134 HN also unassigned), and K138 indicates conformational exchange on the millisecond timescale, forming two dynamic surface patches on the N-terminal saposin-like domain.
anchor: Shaded areas identify residues where no Hn signal could be identified due to extensive line broadening.
locator: Fig. 2B and legend (p. 20533), Results pp. 20532-20535, and Experimental Procedures p. 20529
caveat_note: Same NMR sample of full-length CDNF-(1-161) as r1, but 1H line widths in Fig. 2B were collected at 1 GHz whereas the CDNFSP entry card specifies 800 MHz and sequence_length = 101 (saposin-like domain). Minor internal boundary variations across sections: p. 20529 lists unassigned HN for C11, E12, C14, K15, E16, I69, L70, S71, E72, T74, R75, K101, C132, R133, A134, and K138; pp. 20532-20533 report extreme amide proton line-width broadening for 11-16, 68-73, 88, 99-101, 132-133, and 138; p. 20535 states amide proton resonances of 68-75 were absent due to intermediate chemical exchange (and notes similar absence of alpha-helix 4 NMR signals in an isolated CDNF1-105 construct, Ref. 22 / BMRB 18269).

title: The Solution Structure and Dynamics of Full-length Human Cerebral Dopamine Neurotrophic Factor and Its Neuroprotective Role against α-Synuclein Oligomers.
experiment: Comparison of solution NMR structure ensemble of full-length CDNF (PDB 4BIT; NOESY at 800 MHz and 1 GHz) with X-ray crystal structure of N-terminal CDNF (PDB 2W50)
buffer: 20 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM NaCl, 3 mM NaN3, 1 mM EDTA, and 10% (v/v) D2O
construct_or_mutation: recombinant full-length human CDNF-(1-161) (PDB 4BIT) compared with N-terminal human CDNF-(1-107) (PDB 2W50)
other_conditions: NMR sample (4BIT): 0.65 mM monomeric FL-CDNF at pH 6, 25 °C (20 conformers: global backbone r.m.s.d. = 7.16 ± 1.51 Å, N-terminal domain 10-100 ~1.1 Å, C-terminal domain 110-150 ~0.7 Å; zero interdomain NOEs; 310 helix 95-102 present in 8 out of 20 conformers); X-ray comparison structure (2W50, Ref. 14): dimeric CDNF-(1-107) crystallized in 100 mM sodium acetate pH 4.6, 200 mM ammonium acetate, 25-30% (w/v) MME-PEG 2000; backbone r.m.s.d. between 4BIT and 2W50 over ordered residues 10-62 and 72-100 = 1.15 Å
alt_state_structure: 4BIT: solution NMR ensemble of monomeric full-length CDNF with partially folded alpha-helix 4 (solvent-exposed Ala-66 at 25.1 ± 9.0% and Leu-70 at 36.4 ± 10.0%, buried Thr-67 and Lys-68) and semi-independently oriented domains (Fig. 1, Fig. 3, Table 1); 2W50: X-ray crystal structure of dimeric N-terminal CDNF (residues 1-107) with well-defined alpha-helical residues 65-73 and buried Ala-66 and Leu-70 side chains (Fig. 3, Results)
author_claim: Comparison of monomeric full-length solution structure 4BIT with dimeric N-terminal crystal structure 2W50 shows structural differences concentrated in dynamic segments 1-15, 99-103, and especially alpha-helix 4 residues A65-V73, which sample conformations ranging from partially folded with solvent-exposed hydrophobic A66 and L70 side chains in solution to a well-defined alpha-helix with buried A66 and L70 in the crystal.
anchor: comparison of the three-dimensional structure of full-length CDNF that was solved by solution NMR (shown in blue) with the three-dimensional structure of the N-terminal-truncated CDNF that was solved by x-ray crystallography (shown in red).
locator: Fig. 3 and legend (p. 20534), Results pp. 20531-20535, Discussion p. 20538; conditions: Experimental Procedures p. 20529 and Results p. 20534
caveat_note: Compares full-length CDNF-(1-161) NMR ensemble (PDB 4BIT, pH 6, monomeric) against prior X-ray crystal structure of N-terminal CDNF (PDB 2W50, pH 4.6, dimeric; described as residues 9-107 in Abstract p. 20527 and residues 1-107 on pp. 20528 and 20534), whereas the CDNFSP entry card represents the 101-residue saposin-like domain relaxation entry at 800 MHz, 298.0 K. Oligomeric state and pH differ between 4BIT (monomer, pH 6) and 2W50 (dimer, pH 4.6), which could contribute to conformational and solvent-exposure differences at 65-73. Presence of the 310 helix (95-102) in 8 of 20 NMR conformers reflects conformer bundle frequency rather than a fitted equilibrium population.
